arm-A.title: The Agents seize Neo at the office
arm-A.summary: A cell phone delivered to Neo's cubicle connects him to Morpheus, who warns that the Agents are closing in and guides him through the office as a search closes in. Neo slips past the search into an empty office, where Morpheus directs him to open a window and cross a scaffold to the roof as the only exit. Neo refuses the climb, then attempts it, but the wind knocks him off balance, he drops the phone, and his nerve breaks. He climbs back inside just as a cop reaches the room, and is taken: the Agents lead him handcuffed out of the skyscraper and force him into a dark sedan, while Trinity witnesses the capture in her motorcycle's rearview mirror.
arm-A.action: The event opens with Neo at his cubicle receiving a phone that rings with Morpheus on the line, warning that the Agents are coming and that he does not know what they will do. Neo glimpses Agent Smith, Agent Brown and [...] cops onto the floor, and a female employee points out his cubicle. Following Morpheus's commands, Neo lunges into an empty cubicle, hides while the Agents search his own, then rolls out, freezes behind a cop, and sneaks across the row into an empty office. There Morpheus directs him to open a window and cross a scaffold to the roof; Neo refuses, then relents and climbs onto the ledge, but a blast of wind knocks him off balance, he drops the phone, and he retreats inside just as a cop opens the door. The Agents then lead a handcuffed Neo out of the skyscraper and force him into a dark sedan, while Trinity watches the capture in her motorcycle's rearview mirror and reacts with dismay.

arm-B.title: The Agents seize Neo at the office
arm-B.summary: A phone reaches Neo's cubicle and Morpheus, on the line, warns that forces are closing in and will not say what they intend. Neo sees Agent Smith leading cops onto the floor and a female employee pointing out his cubicle, and he follows Morpheus's instructions out of the row and into an empty office. Morpheus directs him out to a ledge from which he can reach the roof; Neo commits, but his nerve breaks when the wind blasts him and the phone falls from his grip just as a cop opens the door, and he climbs back inside into the hands of the waiting cop. He is seized, handcuffed, and forced into a dark sedan in the Agents' custody. Trinity, watching from her motorcycle, sees him taken and knows the extraction has failed.
arm-B.action: The event folds a raid, a guided escape, and a failed leap into one motion. Neo is converted from a recipient of messages into a fugitive and then into a prisoner: guided out of the cubicle, out to the window ledge, and back inside into Agent Smith's custody. Morpheus's remote guidance gets him out of the row but cannot steady his body at the ledge, and the dropped phone severs his only link to that guidance at the moment he most needs it. The one exit he could not bring himself to take is the only one that would have kept him free.

state_triples.reading: Neo is being tested at every level at once — his body betrays him, his self-image as an insignificant man who did nothing collides with a pursuit that treats him as the most wanted person in the building, and his terror of the ledge blinds him to the fact that capture is the worse fate. He follows Morpheus because the alternative is to stay and find out what 'they' will do, but the moment the choice becomes physical and solitary, the part of him that has always believed he is nobody wins, and he climbs back toward the danger he thinks is survivable. arm-A.title: Neo is reclaimed and taken to Morpheus
arm-A.summary: A ringing phone drags Neo out of a nightmare and a voice names him 'the One,' extracting a single 'Yes' and a destination before the line dies. He crosses the rain-soaked night to the Adams Street bridge, where a car slides to a stop and Trinity pulls him inside. Under Switch's gun, Neo resists the demand to strip for an unknown device and nearly bolts, but Trinity reframes the danger as coming from himself and warns him against a road he already knows — and he closes the door and stays. The car speeds through the dark wet streets with Neo seated, silent, and no longer resisting.

state_triples.reading: Neo moves through the event as a man being reclaimed by a destiny he never asked for and still cannot comprehend. Each surrender is framed — by Morpheus's prophecy, by Trinity's gentleness — as a choice, and he accepts the framing because the alternative (the road he knows, the abyss he has always been running toward) is more terrifying than compliance. He closes the door not out of trust but because staying feels marginally less like falling; the event's quiet horror is that his one act of 'agency' is the surrender of his agency.

arm-B.title: The Bug Removed
arm-B.summary: In the moving car, Trinity seals an extraction device over Neo's navel to pull a tracking bug from his body. arm-B.action: The extraction shifts from persuasion to force. Trinity first tries to coax the bug out with suction while reassuring Neo, but the monitor shows it burrowing deeper and Switch keeps announcing that she is about to lose it. She refuses to let it escape, fires an electric charge into Neo, and holds it through his convulsions until the bug rockets free. Trinity then displays the squirming creature to Neo, rolls down the window, and discards it; the car carries the crew out of the wet streets, vanishing into the rainy night before pulling up behind a forgotten hotel.

He cannot yet know Trinity's cruelty was a desperate medical necessity, so he reads her as someone who hurt him with casual intent — and that misreading binds him to her even as it keeps him wary.

state_triples.reading: Trinity feels the strain of performing a high-stakes procedure on a terrified, unanesthetized man and hates that she must hurt him, yet she treats the electrocution as a medical necessity rather than cruelty — she will harm the person she is saving because losing the bug would expose the crew. Her faith that calm authority can manage Neo keeps getting undercut by the reality that she has to overpower him, and she lets no remorse show until the threat is out and caged.

Switch carries the residual tension of having held Neo at gunpoint and stays locked on the failure mode, calling out that the bug is on the move and that Trinity will lose it — scanning for the disaster while she is locked on the procedure. He reads her approach as failing and Neo as a mere coppertop liability, and both readings are off: the bug really is escaping, which is why she electrocutes Neo, and Neo is a frightened victim of the same system rather than an adversary. Switch is right about the risk but wrong that Trinity can't close it.
